run_2.environment: Separately installed Ubuntu 24.04.4 root filesystem from the original audit

font_substitution_negative_test: Analysis rejected a substitute font with a hash-mismatch error before data extraction.
notes: Two separate R processes in independently installed Ubuntu filesystems on the same underlying host/kernel/hardware; each uses one core.
This font-pinned follow-up reused the installed environments; it was not another installation-from-zero test.
The verification runs were launched concurrently; timings are observations, not benchmarks or hardware requirements.
All 14 CSVs and four PNG files matched byte for byte across these two runs; decoded figure pixels matched too.
The numerical outputs also match the original pre-font-pin published CSVs.
Fonts and PNG backend are pinned, but system graphics libraries are not completely locked; no universal pixel-identity promise.
Windows, macOS, different hardware/physical machines and the RPCA/CCA extensions remain untested.

original_pre_font_pin_clean_install_audi.root_filesystem: Official Ubuntu Base 24.04.4 with no pre-existing R or analysis packages
original_pre_font_pin_clean_install_audi.isolation: Chroot on the same underlying host/kernel/hardware, not a separate physical machine
original_pre_font_pin_clean_install_audi.bootstrap: DNS and device nodes configured; sudo installed, then the documented setup and unmodified analysis ran unchanged
original_pre_font_pin_clean_install_audi.figure_finding: All four PNGs regenerated with matching dimensions but different pixels. Noto Sans versus DejaVu Sans defaults were found; the inspected UMAP showed font/layout differences with byte-identical coordinates, not proof that every changed pixel in all four was font-caused.
